Reproducible single-assay pipelines

pipelines.Rmd

Discover the pipeline after preprocessing

A pipeline records the preprocessing steps applied to an experiment. Start by normalizing and imputing the bundled glycoproteomics experiment with ordinary function calls:

library(glyclean)
#> 
#> Attaching package: 'glyclean'
#> The following object is masked from 'package:stats':
#> 
#>     aggregate

original <- glyexp::as_glycoproteomic_se(glyexp::real_experiment)
#> Warning: replacing previous import 'S4Arrays::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' by
#> 'DelayedArray::makeNindexFromArrayViewport' when loading 'SummarizedExperiment'
cleaned <- normalize_total_area(original)
cleaned <- impute_min_prob(cleaned, q = 0.01, seed = 42)

These calls automatically add a pipeline to the experiment’s metadata. Use get_pipeline() to retrieve it and print the recorded steps:

history <- get_pipeline(cleaned)
history
#> ── <glyclean_pipeline> 2 steps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   1. normalize_total_area
#>      (no parameters)
#>   2. impute_min_prob
#>     by = NULL, q = 0.01, tune.sigma = 1, seed = 42

identical(history, S4Vectors::metadata(cleaned)$pipeline)
#> [1] TRUE

A glyclean_pipeline is a list of steps. Each step contains a function and its parameters, in the order they were applied. The printed summary shows the function names and their parameters.

Automatic functions record the actual functions chosen. For example, auto_normalize() selects median normalization for this glycoproteomics experiment, so its history contains normalize_median():

automatically_normalized <- auto_normalize(original)
#> ℹ Normalization method: `normalize_median()`
#> ℹ Reason: default for "glycoproteomics".
get_pipeline(automatically_normalized)
#> ── <glyclean_pipeline> 1 step ──────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   1. normalize_median
#>      (no parameters)

Reproduce preprocessing from its history

Apply the recorded history to the same original experiment to reproduce the preprocessing exactly:

replayed <- apply_pipeline(original, history)
identical(replayed, cleaned)
#> [1] TRUE
stopifnot(identical(replayed, cleaned))

This compares the whole experiment, including its assay, annotations and pipeline metadata. Exact replay assumes the same original input, package versions and random-number generator configuration; seeds are recorded in the step parameters.

Create a pipeline manually

When you already know the steps you want, define a recipe with glyclean_pipeline(). Omit the experiment argument and use full argument names for any parameters:

recipe <- glyclean_pipeline(
  normalize_total_area(),
  impute_min_prob(q = 0.01, seed = 42)
)
recipe
#> ── <glyclean_pipeline> 2 steps ─────────────────────────────────────────────────
#>   1. normalize_total_area
#>      (no parameters)
#>   2. impute_min_prob
#>     q = 0.01, seed = 42, by = NULL, tune.sigma = 1

Building the recipe does not preprocess any data. Supply the experiment when you apply it:

from_recipe <- apply_pipeline(original, recipe)
identical(from_recipe, cleaned)
#> [1] TRUE
stopifnot(identical(from_recipe, cleaned))

Recipes can also include auto_*() calls to choose methods when they are applied. The resulting experiment’s history records the concrete operations that ran, ready to inspect or replay.

Treat zeros as missing measurements

When zeros in your data represent missing measurements, explicitly convert them before imputation. zero_to_na() changes exact zeros only; it does not change nonzero values or decide how to impute. It is recorded like any other operation:

zero_recipe <- glyclean_pipeline(zero_to_na(), impute_min_prob(seed = 42))
zero_cleaned <- apply_pipeline(original, zero_recipe)
stopifnot(identical(
  apply_pipeline(original, get_pipeline(zero_cleaned)), zero_cleaned
))
